claim: BOP genes are involved in controlling the abundance of PIF4.
source: Here, we present evidence that the BLADE-ON-PETIOLE (BOP) genes, which have previously been shown to control leaf and flower development in Arabidopsis, are involved in controlling the abundance of PIF4.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a main finding of the study.

claim: BOP2 promotes photomorphogenesis by suppressing PIF4 activity.
source: Genetic analysis shows that BOP2 promotes photo-morphogenesis and modulates thermomorphogenesis by suppressing PIF4 activity, through a reduction in PIF4 protein level.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by genetic analysis data.

claim: BOP2 modulates thermomorphogenesis by suppressing PIF4 activity.
source: Genetic analysis shows that BOP2 promotes photo-morphogenesis and modulates thermomorphogenesis by suppressing PIF4 activity, through a reduction in PIF4 protein level.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by genetic analysis data.

claim: BOP2 reduces PIF4 protein level.
source: Genetic analysis shows that BOP2 promotes photo-morphogenesis and modulates thermomorphogenesis by suppressing PIF4 activity, through a reduction in PIF4 protein level.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by protein level measurements.

claim: PIF4 ubiquitination was reduced in the bop2 mutant in red-light-grown seedlings.
source: In red-light-grown seedlings PIF4 ubiquitination was reduced in the bop2 mutant.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by TUBEs assay data.

claim: BOP proteins physically interact with PIF4.
source: Moreover, we found that BOP proteins physically interact with both PIF4 and CULLIN3A and that a CULLIN3-BOP2 complex ubiquitinates PIF4 in vitro.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by co-immunoprecipitation, BiFC, yeast two-hybrid, and in vitro pulldown assays.

claim: BOP proteins physically interact with CULLIN3A.
source: Moreover, we found that BOP proteins physically interact with both PIF4 and CULLIN3A and that a CULLIN3-BOP2 complex ubiquitinates PIF4 in vitro.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by co-immunoprecipitation assays.

claim: A CULLIN3-BOP2 complex ubiquitinates PIF4 in vitro.
source: Moreover, we found that BOP proteins physically interact with both PIF4 and CULLIN3A and that a CULLIN3-BOP2 complex ubiquitinates PIF4 in vitro.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by in vitro ubiquitination assays.

claim: BOP proteins act as substrate adaptors in a CUL3BOP1/BOP2 E3 ubiquitin ligase complex.
source: This shows that BOP proteins act as substrate adaptors in a CUL3BOP1/BOP2 E3 ubiquitin ligase complex, targeting PIF4 proteins for ubiquitination and subsequent degradation.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a conclusion from the experimental data.

claim: The CUL3BOP1/BOP2 E3 ubiquitin ligase complex targets PIF4 proteins for ubiquitination and subsequent degradation.
source: This shows that BOP proteins act as substrate adaptors in a CUL3BOP1/BOP2 E3 ubiquitin ligase complex, targeting PIF4 proteins for ubiquitination and subsequent degradation.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a conclusion from the experimental data.

claim: Phytochrome photoreceptors regulate plant responses to the environment by controlling the abundance of PHYTOCHROME INTERACTING FACTOR (PIF) transcription factors.
source: Phytochrome photoreceptors regulate plant responses to the environment in large part by controlling the abundance of PHYTOCHROME INTERACTING FACTOR (PIF) transcription factors.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as established knowledge.

claim: BOP genes have previously been shown to control leaf and flower development in Arabidopsis.
source: Here, we present evidence that the BLADE-ON-PETIOLE (BOP) genes, which have previously been shown to control leaf and flower development in Arabidopsis, are involved in controlling the abundance of PIF4.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and references prior work.

claim: Members of the phytochrome light receptor family have the unique ability to sense red (R) and far-red (FR) light.
source: Members of the phytochrome light receptor family have the unique ability to sense red (R) and far-red (FR) light.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge.

claim: Phytochromes control germination, early seedling development, stem and internode elongation, the balance between leaf lamina and petiole formation, and the transition to flowering.
source: They control germination, early seedling development, stem and internode elongation, the balance between leaf lamina and petiole formation (part of the shade avoidance syndrome) and the transition to flowering (Franklin and Quail, 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: PhyB is the primary photoreceptor mediating seedling de-etiolation in red light.
source: All higher plants possess multiple phytochromes (phyA-phyE in Arabidopsis) with phyB being the primary photoreceptor mediating seedling de-etiolation in red light.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge.

claim: A major function of phyB is to prevent the shade-avoidance syndrome (SAS) in sunlight.
source: A major function of phyB is to prevent the shade-avoidance syndrome (SAS) in sunlight, an environment that is rich in red light and thus leading to phyB activation.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge.

claim: In Arabidopsis phyB controls the SAS with major contributions from phyD and phyE.
source: In Arabidopsis phyB controls the SAS with major contributions from phyD and phyE (Devlin et al., 1998).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: PhyB can integrate light and temperature signals by acting as a thermosensor.
source: Recently, it was also shown that phyB can integrate light and temperature signals by acting as a thermosensor (Jung et al., 2016; Legris et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: Once activated, phytochromes are transported from the cytosol to the nucleus.
source: Once activated, phytochromes are transported from the cytosol to the nucleus, where they interact with a group of transcription factors from the Phytocrome Interacting Factor (PIF) family (Leivar and Monte, 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: Phytochromes interact with transcription factors from the Phytochrome Interacting Factor (PIF) family in the nucleus.
source: Once activated, phytochromes are transported from the cytosol to the nucleus, where they interact with a group of transcription factors from the Phytocrome Interacting Factor (PIF) family (Leivar and Monte, 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: PIFs act as inhibitors of phytochrome-induced responses in a partially redundant manner.
source: PIFs act as inhibitors of phytochrome-induced responses in a partially redundant manner and the phytochromes promote these responses by inhibiting the PIFs (Lorrain et al., 2009; Leivar et al., 2008b; Leivar et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: Phytochromes promote responses by inhibiting the PIFs.
source: PIFs act as inhibitors of phytochrome-induced responses in a partially redundant manner and the phytochromes promote these responses by inhibiting the PIFs (Lorrain et al., 2009; Leivar et al., 2008b; Leivar et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: Different members of the PIF family display different functions in light and temperature regulated development.
source: Different members of the PIF family display different functions in light and temperature regulated development.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge.

claim: PIF1 is a repressor of seed germination.
source: For instance, PIF1 is a repressor of seed germination (Oh et al., 2004), PIF4 plays a crucial role in the response to high temperature (Koini et al., 2009) and PIF4 and PIF5 induce leaf senescence in Arabidopsis (Sakuraba et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: PIF4 plays a crucial role in the response to high temperature.
source: For instance, PIF1 is a repressor of seed germination (Oh et al., 2004), PIF4 plays a crucial role in the response to high temperature (Koini et al., 2009) and PIF4 and PIF5 induce leaf senescence in Arabidopsis (Sakuraba et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: PIF4 and PIF5 induce leaf senescence in Arabidopsis.
source: For instance, PIF1 is a repressor of seed germination (Oh et al., 2004), PIF4 plays a crucial role in the response to high temperature (Koini et al., 2009) and PIF4 and PIF5 induce leaf senescence in Arabidopsis (Sakuraba et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: PIF4, PIF5 and PIF7 promote elongation of hypocotyls and petioles in response to shade cues.
source: PIF4, PIF5 and PIF7 promote elongation of hypocotyls and petioles in response to shade cues (low R:FR and low blue light) (Lorrain et al., 2008; Keller et al., 2011; Li et al., 2012; de Wit et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: PIFs display different modes of regulation at the transcriptional and post-transcriptional levels.
source: PIFs also display different modes of regulation at the transcriptional and post-transcriptional levels.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge.

claim: Phosphorylation of all studied PIFs is light regulated and in most cases lead to rapid protein degradation.
source: For instance, phosphorylation of all studied PIFs is light regulated and in most cases lead to rapid protein degradation (Leivar and Monte, 2014; Ni et al., 2013; Leivar et al., 2008a).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: Phytochromes may phosphorylate the PIFs.
source: A recent paper suggests that phytochromes may phosphorylate the PIFs (Shin et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: The BR signaling kinase BRASSINOSTEROID-INSENSITIVE2 (BIN2) has been shown to phosphorylate PIF4 and subsequently affect PIF4 protein abundance, but in a non-light-inducible manner.
source: Also, the BR signaling kinase BRASSINOSTEROID-INSENSITIVE2 (BIN2) has been shown to phosphorylate PIF4 and subsequently affect PIF4 protein abundance, but in a non-light-inducible manner (Bernardo-García et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: The degradation of PIF3 by light was reported to be mediated by the Light Response Bric-a-Brack/Tramtrack/Broad (BTB) proteins (LRBs) interacting with Cullin3 (CUL3).
source: As for ubiquitin E3 ligases, the degradation of PIF3 by light was reported to be mediated by the Light Response Bric-a-Brack/Tramtrack/Broad (BTB) proteins (LRBs) interacting with Cullin3 (CUL3), while PIF1 degradation is controlled by a CUL4-COP1-SPA complex (Ni et al., 2014; Zhu et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: PIF1 degradation is controlled by a CUL4-COP1-SPA complex.
source: As for ubiquitin E3 ligases, the degradation of PIF3 by light was reported to be mediated by the Light Response Bric-a-Brack/Tramtrack/Broad (BTB) proteins (LRBs) interacting with Cullin3 (CUL3), while PIF1 degradation is controlled by a CUL4-COP1-SPA complex (Ni et al., 2014; Zhu et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: The degradation of different PIF proteins might be controlled by specific E3 ligase complexes.
source: These findings suggest that the degradation of different PIF proteins might be controlled by specific E3 ligase complexes.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as an inference from cited findings.

claim: Which E3 ligases that control PIF4 degradation has so far been unknown.
source: However, which E3 ligases that control PIF4 degradation has so far been unknown.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a knowledge gap.

claim: The CUL3-based E3 ligase complexes are composed of a CUL3 backbone, an E2-Ub-docking RING Box1 (RBX1) protein and a member from the large family of BTB-domain containing proteins that serve as target-recognition adaptors.
source: The CUL3-based E3 ligase complexes are composed of a CUL3 backbone, an E2-Ub-docking RING Box1 (RBX1) protein and a member from the large family of BTB-domain containing proteins that serve as target-recognition adaptors (Genschik et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: The Arabidopsis genome contains two CUL3 genes, called CUL3A and CUL3B.
source: The Arabidopsis genome contains two CUL3 genes, called CUL3A and CUL3B and about 80 genes encoding BTB domain proteins, which could be possible interactors with CUL3A and CUL3B (Genschik et al., 2013; Gingerich et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: The Arabidopsis genome contains about 80 genes encoding BTB domain proteins.
source: The Arabidopsis genome contains two CUL3 genes, called CUL3A and CUL3B and about 80 genes encoding BTB domain proteins, which could be possible interactors with CUL3A and CUL3B (Genschik et al., 2013; Gingerich et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: NONEXPRESSER OF PR GENES3 and 4 (NPR3 and 4) were shown to function as substrate adaptors in a CUL3 E3 ubiquitin ligase complex to mediate degradation of the co-transcription factor NPR1.
source: Besides LRBs proteins, two other BTB domain containing proteins, NONEXPRESSER OF PR GENES3 and 4 (NPR3 and 4), were shown to function as substrate adaptors in a CUL3 E3 ubiquitin ligase complex to mediate degradation of the co-transcription factor NPR1 (Fu et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: BOP1 and BOP2 are close homologs of NPR proteins.
source: Two close homologs of NPR proteins, BOP1 and BOP2, were previously shown to redundantly regulate leaf development (Ha et al., 2003; Hepworth et al., 2005; Norberg et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: BOP1 and BOP2 redundantly regulate leaf development.
source: Two close homologs of NPR proteins, BOP1 and BOP2, were previously shown to redundantly regulate leaf development (Ha et al., 2003; Hepworth et al., 2005; Norberg et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: In Arabidopsis bop1 bop2 double mutants the leaf lamina extends along the petioles and leaves one and two become massively elongated.
source: In Arabidopsis bop1 bop2 double mutants the leaf lamina extends along the petioles and leaves one and two become massively elongated (Ha et al., 2003; Hepworth et al., 2005; Norberg et al., 2005), phenotypic alterations that are reminiscent of responses to changes in light quality and light intensity (Franklin and Quail, 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: bop1 bop2 double mutants are defective in the suppression of bract formation.
source: bop1 bop2 double mutants are also defective in the suppression of bract formation, do not form floral organ abscission zones and display alterations in floral organ identity and positioning (Hepworth et al., 2005; Norberg et al., 2005; McKim et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: bop1 bop2 double mutants do not form floral organ abscission zones.
source: bop1 bop2 double mutants are also defective in the suppression of bract formation, do not form floral organ abscission zones and display alterations in floral organ identity and positioning (Hepworth et al., 2005; Norberg et al., 2005; McKim et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: bop1 bop2 double mutants display alterations in floral organ identity and positioning.
source: bop1 bop2 double mutants are also defective in the suppression of bract formation, do not form floral organ abscission zones and display alterations in floral organ identity and positioning (Hepworth et al., 2005; Norberg et al., 2005; McKim et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: BOP proteins have been suggested to act as co-transcription factors.
source: The molecular function of BOP proteins is not known but they have been suggested to act as co-transcription factors (Khan et al., 2014) or to inhibit transport of transcription factors to the nucleus (Shimada et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: BOP proteins have been suggested to inhibit transport of transcription factors to the nucleus.
source: The molecular function of BOP proteins is not known but they have been suggested to act as co-transcription factors (Khan et al., 2014) or to inhibit transport of transcription factors to the nucleus (Shimada et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: BOP proteins act as substrate adaptors in a CUL3 E3 ligase complex to control the degradation of PIF4.
source: In this study, we report that BOP proteins act as substrate adaptors in a CUL3 E3 ligase complex to control the degradation of PIF4.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a main finding of the study.

claim: BOP regulatory activity has a strong influence on the role of PIF4 during responses to light and temperature.
source: This regulatory activity has a strong influence on the role of PIF4 during responses to light and temperature.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a conclusion from the study.

claim: The bop1 mutant responded identically to the wild type in all light qualities tested.
source: In all light qualities, the bop1 mutant, bop1-5 (Norberg et al., 2005), responded identically to the wild type (Col-0) control (Figure 1a,b; Figure 1—figure supplement 1a–c).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 1.

claim: The bop2 mutant showed increased elongation in red light compared to Col-0.
source: In contrast, the bop2 mutant, bop2-2 (Hepworth et al., 2005; Norberg et al., 2005), showed increased elongation in red light compared to Col-0, while it displayed slightly increased elongation in white light at lower intensity and no hyposensitivity to blue and far-red light (Figure 1a,b; Figure 1—figure supplement 1a–c).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 1.

claim: The bop2 mutant displayed slightly increased elongation in white light at lower intensity.
source: In contrast, the bop2 mutant, bop2-2 (Hepworth et al., 2005; Norberg et al., 2005), showed increased elongation in red light compared to Col-0, while it displayed slightly increased elongation in white light at lower intensity and no hyposensitivity to blue and far-red light (Figure 1a,b; Figure 1—figure supplement 1a–c).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 1.

claim: The bop2 mutant showed no hyposensitivity to blue and far-red light.
source: In contrast, the bop2 mutant, bop2-2 (Hepworth et al., 2005; Norberg et al., 2005), showed increased elongation in red light compared to Col-0, while it displayed slightly increased elongation in white light at lower intensity and no hyposensitivity to blue and far-red light (Figure 1a,b; Figure 1—figure supplement 1a–c).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 1.

claim: The bop1 bop2 double mutant behaved identically to the bop2 single mutant in hypocotyl elongation experiments.
source: In all these experiments, the bop1 bop2 double mutant behaved identically to the bop2 single mutant, suggesting that only BOP2 plays a significant role in the light-dependent suppression of hypocotyl elongation.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by experimental data.

claim: Only BOP2 plays a significant role in the light-dependent suppression of hypocotyl elongation.
source: In all these experiments, the bop1 bop2 double mutant behaved identically to the bop2 single mutant, suggesting that only BOP2 plays a significant role in the light-dependent suppression of hypocotyl elongation.
evidence: This is stated in the results as an inference from experimental data.

claim: The bop2 and bop1 bop2 mutants displayed significantly decreased cotyledon separation in red light.
source: The bop2 and bop1 bop2 mutants displayed significantly decreased cotyledon separation in red light, with a much stronger alteration in the double mutant (Figure 1c).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 1c.

claim: The bop1 bop2 double mutant showed a slightly delayed hook opening compared to wild type and the single mutants.
source: The bop1 bop2 double mutant showed a slightly delayed hook opening compared to wild type and the single mutants (Figure 1—figure supplement 1d).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1d.

claim: BOP1 and BOP2 have a partially redundant role in cotyledon separation and hook opening.
source: These results suggest a partially redundant role of BOP1 and BOP2 in cotyledon separation and hook opening.
evidence: This is stated in the results as an inference from experimental data.

claim: 35S::BOP1 and 35S::BOP2 seedlings displayed reduced hypocotyl elongation at all red light fluence rates tested, and also in darkness.
source: Interestingly, plants overexpressing BOP genes had the opposite phenotype with both 35S::BOP1 and 35S::BOP2 seedlings displaying reduced hypocotyl elongation at all red light fluence rates tested, and also in darkness (Figure 1—figure supplement 2a,b).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: The bop1-6D mutant showed an opposite cotyledon separating phenotype with a slightly decreased hook folding in darkness.
source: Kinematic analysis also showed an opposite cotyledon separating phenotype in the bop1-6D mutant, a strong activation-tagged line (Norberg et al., 2005), with a slightly decreased hook folding in darkness (Figure 1—figure supplement 2c,d).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: 35S::BOP2 seedlings had a striking hook folding defect in darkness.
source: The 35S::BOP2 seedlings had a striking hook folding defect in darkness (Figure 1—figure supplement 2d), showing that upon over-expression BOP2 can promote photomorphogenesis in the absence of light.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2d.

claim: Upon over-expression BOP2 can promote photomorphogenesis in the absence of light.
source: The 35S::BOP2 seedlings had a striking hook folding defect in darkness (Figure 1—figure supplement 2d), showing that upon over-expression BOP2 can promote photomorphogenesis in the absence of light.
evidence: This is stated in the results as an inference from experimental data.

claim: BOP2, and to a lesser extent BOP1, suppress hypocotyl elongation and promote cotyledon opening, especially in red light conditions.
source: Collectively, our data provide genetic evidence that BOP2, and to a lesser extent BOP1, suppress hypocotyl elongation and promotes cotyledon opening, especially in red light conditions.
evidence: This is stated in the results as a conclusion from experimental data.

claim: The phyB bop2 double mutant showed the same hyposensitive response as the phyB single mutant.
source: The phyB bop2 double mutant showed the same hyposensitive response as the phyB single mutant, suggesting that BOP2 acts in the phyB pathway to suppress hypocotyl elongation in red light (Figure 1—figure supplement 3a).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3a.

claim: BOP2 acts in the phyB pathway to suppress hypocotyl elongation in red light.
source: The phyB bop2 double mutant showed the same hyposensitive response as the phyB single mutant, suggesting that BOP2 acts in the phyB pathway to suppress hypocotyl elongation in red light (Figure 1—figure supplement 3a).
evidence: This is stated in the results as an inference from genetic interaction data.

claim: phyB accumulated to normal levels in bop2.
source: We found that phyB accumulated to normal levels in bop2 suggesting that BOP2 is rather involved in phyB signaling (Figure 1—figure supplement 3b,c).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by western blot data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3b,c.

claim: BOP2 is involved in phyB signaling.
source: We found that phyB accumulated to normal levels in bop2 suggesting that BOP2 is rather involved in phyB signaling (Figure 1—figure supplement 3b,c).
evidence: This is stated in the results as an inference from protein level data.

claim: PIF transcription factors are important mediators of phytochrome signaling.
source: PIF transcription factors are important mediators of phytochrome signaling and PIF4 plays a prominent role during de-etiolation in red light (Huq and Quail, 2002).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by a citation.

claim: PIF4 plays a prominent role during de-etiolation in red light.
source: PIF transcription factors are important mediators of phytochrome signaling and PIF4 plays a prominent role during de-etiolation in red light (Huq and Quail, 2002).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by a citation.

claim: Both the pif4bop2 double mutants and the pif4bop1bop2 triple mutants had the same short hypocotyl as the pif4 single mutant.
source: Interestingly, both the pif4bop2 double mutants and the pif4bop1bop2 triple mutants had the same short hypocotyl as the pif4 single mutant (Figure 2a,b; Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 2.

claim: The pif4 mutants showed more separated cotyledons in response to red light compared to wild type.
source: In the kinematic analysis, compared to wild type the pif4 mutants showed more separated cotyledons in response to red light (Figure 2c).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 2c.

claim: The pif4bop1bop2 triple mutants had the same cotyledon separation phenotype as the pif4 single mutant.
source: As observed for hypocotyl elongation, the pif4bop1bop2 triple mutants had the same cotyledon separation phenotype as the pif4 single mutant (Figure 2c).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 2c.

claim: pif4 is epistatic over bop2.
source: These results show that pif4 is epistatic over bop2 and that PIF4 is necessary for the BOP2-mediated suppression of hypocotyl elongation and promotion of cotyledon separation.
evidence: This is stated in the results as a conclusion from genetic interaction data.

claim: PIF4 is necessary for the BOP2-mediated suppression of hypocotyl elongation and promotion of cotyledon separation.
source: These results show that pif4 is epistatic over bop2 and that PIF4 is necessary for the BOP2-mediated suppression of hypocotyl elongation and promotion of cotyledon separation.
evidence: This is stated in the results as a conclusion from genetic interaction data.

claim: PIF4p::PIF4-HA complemented the pif4 mutant phenotype.
source: PIF4p::PIF4-HA complemented the pif4 mutant phenotype (Figure 3a,b).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 3a,b.

claim: The level of PIF4-HA rapidly decreased in response to red light.
source: As previously observed, the level of PIF4-HA rapidly decreased in response to red light (Figure 3c) (Lorrain et al., 2008; Nozue et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 3c and citations.

claim: In the pif4bop2 mutant background red light led to a slower decline of PIF4-HA levels than in pif4.
source: Interestingly, in the pif4bop2 mutant background red light led to a slower decline of PIF4-HA levels than in pif4 (Figure 3c).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 3c.

claim: After 10 min of red light treatment about 30% of PIF4-HA protein remained in the pif4 background compared to darkness, while more than 80% of PIF4-HA remained in the pif4 bop2 mutant.
source: After 10 min of treatment about 30% of PIF4-HA protein remained in the pif4 background compared to darkness, while more than 80% of PIF4-HA remained in the pif4 bop2 mutant (Figure 3d).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by quantification data shown in Figure 3d.

claim: Changes in PIF4-HA accumulation in pif4bop2 were not due to an effect on PIF4 transcription.
source: These changes in PIF4-HA accumulation in pif4bop2 were not due to an effect on PIF4 transcription as PIF4 transcript levels in the same experimental conditions were the same in both genotypes (Figure 3e).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by transcript level data shown in Figure 3e.

claim: BOP2 controls PIF4 protein abundance in particular during the transition from dark to light conditions.
source: Collectively, these results suggest that BOP2 controls PIF4 protein abundance in particular during the transition from dark to light conditions.
evidence: This is stated in the results as a conclusion from experimental data.

claim: PIF4 undergoes proteasome-mediated degradation when etiolated seedlings are transferred into the light.
source: PIF4 undergoes proteasome-mediated degradation when etiolated seedlings are transferred into the light (Lorrain et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by a citation.

claim: BOP proteins contain BTB domains.
source: Moreover, BOP proteins contain BTB domains, a domain which in other proteins mediates the formation of CUL3-BTB complexes (Geyer et al., 2003; Moon et al., 2004; Pintard et al., 2004).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by citations.

claim: BTB domains in other proteins mediate the formation of CUL3-BTB complexes.
source: Moreover, BOP proteins contain BTB domains, a domain which in other proteins mediates the formation of CUL3-BTB complexes (Geyer et al., 2003; Moon et al., 2004; Pintard et al., 2004).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by citations.

claim: HA-CUL3A co-immunoprecipitated together with both myc-BOP1 and myc-BOP2.
source: HA-CUL3A co-immunoprecipitated together with both myc-BOP1 and myc-BOP2 (Figure 4a) and CUL3A could also be co-immunoprecipitated from 35S::myc-BOP2 plants (Figure 4—figure supplement 1a) indicating that the proteins indeed interact.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by co-IP data shown in Figure 4a.

claim: CUL3A could be co-immunoprecipitated from 35S::myc-BOP2 plants.
source: HA-CUL3A co-immunoprecipitated together with both myc-BOP1 and myc-BOP2 (Figure 4a) and CUL3A could also be co-immunoprecipitated from 35S::myc-BOP2 plants (Figure 4—figure supplement 1a) indicating that the proteins indeed interact.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by co-IP data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1a.

claim: CUL3A interacted more strongly with BOP2 than with BOP1.
source: In general, CUL3A interacted more strongly with BOP2 than with BOP1 (Figure 4a).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by co-IP data shown in Figure 4a.

claim: BOP1 and BOP2 may act as substrate adaptors in a CUL3BOP1/BOP2 E3 ubiquitin ligase complex.
source: These findings indicate that BOP1 and BOP2 may act as substrate adaptors in a CUL3BOP1/BOP2 E3 ubiquitin ligase complex.

claim: HA-PIF4 co-immunoprecipitated with both myc-BOP1 and myc-BOP2.
source: HA-PIF4 was found to co-immunoprecipitate with both myc-BOP1 and myc-BOP2 (Figure 4b).

claim: The interaction between BOP2 and PIF4 was confirmed in vivo using Bimolecular Fluorescence Complementation.

claim: A strong signal could be seen in nuclear bodies which were previously observed in PIF4 and phytochrome localization experiments.

claim: The BOP2-PIF4 interaction was detected using both LacZ and histidine auxotrophy as reporters of the interaction in yeast two hybrid assays.

evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by yeast two-hybrid data shown in Figure 4d.

claim: Glutathione S-transferase (GST) tagged PIF4 directly interacted with maltose-binding protein (MBP) tagged BOP2, but not with MBP alone.

claim: Both HA-CUL3A and HA-PIF4 could be pulled down by BOP2.

claim: All three proteins (CUL3A, BOP2, and PIF4) may act in the same complex.

claim: The BOP proteins physically interact with PIF4 and serve as substrate adaptors in a CUL3BOP1/BOP2 E3 ubiquitin ligase complex potentially targeting PIF4 for ubiquitination and subsequent degradation.

claim: A set of closely migrating high molecular weight proteins were observed in red light treated seedlings, indicating a light induced polyubiquitination of PIF4-HA.
source: A set of closely migrating high molecular weight proteins were observed in red light treated seedlings, indicating a light induced polyubiquitination of PIF4-HA (Figure 5a, Figure 5—figure supplement 1).

claim: Significantly reduced polyubiquitination of PIF4-HA was observed in the bop2 mutant background.
source: Significantly reduced polyubiquitination of PIF4-HA was observed in the bop2 mutant background (Figure 5a,b Figure 5—source data 1), indicating that in vivo BOP2 promotes polyubiquitination of PIF4 in response to red light.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by TUBEs assay data shown in Figure 5a,b.

claim: In vivo BOP2 promotes polyubiquitination of PIF4 in response to red light.

evidence: This is stated in the results as a conclusion from TUBEs assay data.

claim: Ubiquitinated GST-PIF4 was only observed in the presence of MBP-BOP2.
source: Furthermore, ubiquitinated GST-PIF4 was only observed in the presence of MBP-BOP2.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by in vitro ubiquitination assay data.

claim: BOP2 possesses the capacity to directly ubiquitinate PIF4.
source: These data demonstrate that BOP2 possesses the capacity to directly ubiquitinate PIF4.

claim: The CUL3BOP1/BOP2 E3 ubiquitin ligase complex controls PIF4 protein levels.
source: Collectively, our results indicate that the CUL3BOP1/BOP2 E3 ubiquitin ligase complex controls PIF4 protein levels (Figures 3–5).

claim: PIF4 is known to play a key role in the response to warm temperatures.
source: In addition to its role in light signaling, PIF4 is known to play a key role in the response to warm temperatures (Koini et al., 2009; Johansson et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by citations.

claim: At 22°C, hypocotyl length of all tested mutants (pif4, bop1, bop2, and bop1bop2) was indistinguishable from the wild type in constant white light.
source: In constant white light, hypocotyl length of all tested mutants, pif4, bop1, bop2, and bop1bop2, was indistinguishable from the wild type at 22°C (Figure 6a).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 6a.

claim: At 28°C the hypocotyls of bop1 and bop2 mutants were longer than the wild type.
source: However, at 28°C the hypocotyls of bop1 and bop2 mutants were longer than the wild type while in pif4 mutants the temperature response was largely abolished (Figure 6a).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 6a.

claim: In pif4 mutants the temperature response was largely abolished.
source: However, at 28°C the hypocotyls of bop1 and bop2 mutants were longer than the wild type while in pif4 mutants the temperature response was largely abolished (Figure 6a).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 6a.

claim: Overexpression of BOP1 or BOP2 strongly suppressed hypocotyl elongation at 28°C.
source: On the contrary, overexpression of BOP1 or BOP2 strongly suppressed hypocotyl elongation at 28°C (Figure 6a).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 6a.

claim: The bop1bop2 double mutant displayed an enhanced phenotype compared to bop1 and bop2 single mutants in response to temperature.
source: Interestingly, the bop1bop2 double mutant displayed an enhanced phenotype compared to bop1 and bop2 single mutants, indicating that, in contrast to the light response, BOP1 and BOP2 function in a partially redundant manner in response to temperature.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by experimental data.

claim: In contrast to the light response, BOP1 and BOP2 function in a partially redundant manner in response to temperature.
source: Interestingly, the bop1bop2 double mutant displayed an enhanced phenotype compared to bop1 and bop2 single mutants, indicating that, in contrast to the light response, BOP1 and BOP2 function in a partially redundant manner in response to temperature.
evidence: This is stated in the results as an inference from experimental data.

claim: The pif4 phenotype was epistatic over the bop2 single mutant and the bop1bop2 double mutant in both growth conditions.
source: Importantly, as observed for the red light responses, the pif4 phenotype was epistatic over the bop2 single mutant and the bop1bop2 double mutant in both growth conditions (Figure 6a, Figure 6—figure supplement 1a), suggesting that the longer hypocotyls in bop mutants is due to elevated PIF4 levels.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 6a and Figure 6—figure supplement 1a.

claim: The longer hypocotyls in bop mutants is due to elevated PIF4 levels.
source: Importantly, as observed for the red light responses, the pif4 phenotype was epistatic over the bop2 single mutant and the bop1bop2 double mutant in both growth conditions (Figure 6a, Figure 6—figure supplement 1a), suggesting that the longer hypocotyls in bop mutants is due to elevated PIF4 levels.
evidence: This is stated in the results as an inference from genetic interaction data.

claim: The level of PIF4-HA dramatically increased in response to high temperature.
source: As previously observed, the level of PIF4-HA dramatically increased in response to high temperature (Figure 6b,c) (Johansson et al., 2014; Oh et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by western blot data shown in Figure 6b,c and citations.

claim: Higher abundance of PIF4-HA was observed in the pif4 bop2 background compared to the pif4 background at both 22°C and 28°C.
source: Consistent with the red light response, higher abundance of PIF4-HA was observed in the pif4 bop2 background compared to the pif4 background at both 22°C and 28°C (Figure 6b,c).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by western blot data shown in Figure 6b,c.

claim: The longer hypocotyls of bop1-5 mutants under 12/12 hr growth conditions could be linked to increased levels of PIF4.
source: We also showed that the longer hypocotyls of bop1-5 mutants under 12/12 hr growth conditions (Figure 6—figure supplement 1a) could be linked to increased levels of PIF4 (Figure 6—figure supplement 1c,d) confirming that BOP1 and BOP2 have partially overlapping functions during these conditions.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: BOP1 and BOP2 have partially overlapping functions during 12/12 hr growth conditions.
source: We also showed that the longer hypocotyls of bop1-5 mutants under 12/12 hr growth conditions (Figure 6—figure supplement 1a) could be linked to increased levels of PIF4 (Figure 6—figure supplement 1c,d) confirming that BOP1 and BOP2 have partially overlapping functions during these conditions.
evidence: This is stated in the results as a conclusion from experimental data.

claim: High temperature increases the rate of reversion from the active Pfr form to the inactive Pr form of phyB.
source: One recent study has shown that high temperature increases the rate of reversion from the active Pfr form to the inactive Pr form of phyB (Jung et al., 2016; Legris et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by citations.

claim: PfrB (phyB in the Pfr form) promotes PIF4 degradation.
source: As PfrB (phyB in the Pfr form) promotes PIF4 degradation (Leivar et al., 2008b; Leivar et al., 2012), our findings suggest that the longer hypocotyls in bop mutants at high temperature result from enhanced PIF4 accumulation due to reduced PfrB and reduced BOP-mediated degradation.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by citations.

claim: The longer hypocotyls in bop mutants at high temperature result from enhanced PIF4 accumulation due to reduced PfrB and reduced BOP-mediated degradation.
source: As PfrB (phyB in the Pfr form) promotes PIF4 degradation (Leivar et al., 2008b; Leivar et al., 2012), our findings suggest that the longer hypocotyls in bop mutants at high temperature result from enhanced PIF4 accumulation due to reduced PfrB and reduced BOP-mediated degradation.
evidence: This is stated in the results as an inference from experimental data and cited knowledge.

claim: BOP-mediated control of PIF4 abundance is important to control not only the light-mediated but also the temperature-mediated growth response in Arabidopsis.
source: All together, these data suggest that BOP-mediated control of PIF4 abundance is important to control not only the light-mediated but also the temperature-mediated growth response in Arabidopsis.
evidence: This is stated in the results as a conclusion from experimental data.

claim: PIF4 is now established as a central component in the regulation of plant growth in response to many different environmental and hormonal signaling pathways.
source: PIF4 is now established as a central component in the regulation of plant growth in response to many different environmental and hormonal signaling pathways, such as the response to light, temperature, gibberellins and brassinolides (Sakuraba et al., 2014; Bernardo-García et al., 2014; Johansson et al., 2014; Oh et al., 2012; Lucyshyn and Wigge, 2009; Sun et al., 2013; Li et al., 2016; Pedmale et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by citations.

claim: For light signaling it has been known for quite some time that this involves the regulation of PIF4 stability through ubiquitination targeting the protein for degradation.
source: For light signaling it has been known for quite some time that this involves the regulation of PIF4 stability through ubiquitination targeting the protein for degradation (Lorrain et al., 2009; Lorrain et al., 2008).

claim: The nature of the E3 ligase complex mediating PIF4 ubiquitination has been unknown.
source: However, the nature of the E3 ligase complex mediating this ubiquitination has been unknown.

claim: BOP-mediated regulation has a significant contribution in regulating the levels of PIF4 particularly during de-etiolation in red light and when growing plants at elevated temperatures.

claim: Other E3 ligases or proteases are likely to contribute since PIF4 ubiquitination and degradation is not completely abolished in bop mutants.

claim: The CUL3-BOP E3 ubiquitin ligase might also be involved in the regulation of PIF4 protein stability in the dark.

claim: BOP2 plays a less pleiotropic role in the control of de-etiolation than LRBs and SPAs.

claim: BOPs sometimes work as homodimers, which would explain the unique role of BOP2 in controlling red light suppression of hypocotyl elongation.

claim: BOP1 and BOP2 can work as heterodimers to control other environmental response, which would explain the role of both BOP1 and BOP2 in controlling high temperature induction of hypocotyl elongation.
